To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

instructed attention to emotional stimuli during working memory encoding results in enhanced performance, as indexed by increased memory performance, reduced reaction times, and enhanced recognition memory performance for positive pictures, compared to passive processing.
attention to emotion enhances memory performance, while emotional distraction impairs it, and that these behavioral effects are associated with distinct patterns of brain activation.

instructed attention to emotional information during WM encoding results in enhanced performance, and that a network of regions including the prefrontal cortic, the insula, the amygdala, the parahippoocampal gyris and the fusiform gyrus is involved in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the brain controls attention and how this control is influenced by emotional stimuli.
understanding the mechanisms of emotional distraction in working memory and how attentional instructions can modulate this process.
the neural and behavioral consequences of attention to emotional stimuli during working memory encoding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain regions involved in instructed attention to emotional information during WM encoding are the same as those involved in attention to non-emotional information.
the brain processes underlying the ability to attend to task-relevant information while filtering out task-irrelevant information are complex, involving a distributed network of brain regions.

the neural and behavioral consequences of attentional control during encoding of emotional information in working memory are dependent on task demands, and that attentional control is associated with enhanced performance and reduced emotional distraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

attention to emotional information during WM encoding is associated with a network of brain regions, which includes regions that have been previously implicated in emotional distraction and regions associated with cognitive control.
attentional control of emotional information during encoding is a dynamic and complex process involving multiple brain regions.
instructed attention to emotional stimuli enhances memory performance, while emotional distraction impairs memory performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neural network underlying instructed attention to emotional information is distinct from the neural network underlying emotional distraction, and that these networks are associated with WM and recognition memory processes.

the neural network involved in attending to emotional information while filtering out task-irrelevant information is largely overlapping with the network that is activated during emotional distraction, suggesting that the brain is not able to distinguish between the two conditions.
attentional control and emotion are tightly coupled and that this coupling is reflected in the neural networks underlying attentional control.
